papers.title: Characterizing transition state in mouse vigilance with electroencephalogram-electromyogram hypnodensity.
papers.summary: This study characterized the temporal dynamics of sleep-wake transitions in mice using EEG/EMG recordings and expert annotations, finding that NREMS-to-REMS transitions are longest and REMS-to-NREMS transitions are most abrupt, and developed SVM classifiers that predict transition midpoints with moderate inter-rater reliability, providing a reproducible framework for quantifying transitions.

papers.title: Diurnal time and sleep pressure modulate cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations in synchrony with wake-promoting nuclei
papers.summary: Using a 34-hour sleep deprivation study with fMRI/EEG/NIRS, this work shows that CSF low-frequency oscillations at vasomotor frequencies increase with time awake and show diurnal fluctuations peaking in early morning, and are associated with vigilance and reticular activating system activity but not plasma norepinephrine or EEG slow waves, indicating independent modulation by sleep pressure and diurnal time.

papers.title: REM Sleep Disengagement of β Oscillations Permits Rapid Dream Movements in Parkinsonism
papers.summary: In non-human primates, MPTP-induced parkinsonism enhanced beta oscillations and impaired movement-related neural dynamics during wake and NREM sleep, but these were attenuated during REM sleep with beta suppression preceding REM onset, demonstrating that parkinsonian network dysfunction is dynamically gated by brain state and revealing a latent capacity for rapid movement during REM.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Face-Validity Indicators in Automatically Detected Dog Sleep Spindles.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis validated a dog sleep spindle detection algorithm by checking automatically detected spindles against three face validity criteria from human EEG, finding that most data sets met criteria for event shortness, midline distribution, and amplitude-negative chirp association, supporting the dog as a model for sleep spindle research and the quality of the detection method.

papers.title: Automated autism spectrum disorder detection using EEG signals and time-frequency visibility graphs.
papers.summary: This study proposed a dual-domain framework for automated ASD detection using EEG, combining time-frequency decompositions (STFT, DWT, WVD, SLT) with Horizontal Visibility Graph features and machine learning classifiers, with the DWT-HVG and Soft Voting Ensemble achieving 93.54% accuracy and 98.17% AUC, outperforming other methods and providing an efficient objective screening tool.

papers.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: This study adapted a deep neural network (U-Sleep) for automated sleep staging in Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, achieving human-level agreement after finetuning on multicenter datasets and improving REM detection precision with confidence thresholds.

papers.title: Leednet: a lightweight network for event detection in EEG signals.
papers.summary: The authors propose LEEDNet, a lightweight convolutional network for EEG event detection, which outperformed state-of-the-art baselines on the NMT-Events dataset with only 0.25M parameters, showing that raw EEG input is sufficient and more efficient than handcrafted features.

papers.title: Chronic corticosterone exposure disrupts bile acids homeostasis associated with circadian dysfunction in the liver of chickens.
papers.summary: In chickens, chronic corticosterone exposure disrupted hepatic circadian clock genes and bile acid homeostasis, altering rhythms, reducing total bile acids at ZT18, and increasing gallbladder bile acids at ZT22, with in vitro evidence that glucocorticoids enhance MRP2-mediated bile acid efflux.

papers.title: Respiratory phase shapes brain-heart dynamics: evidence from recurrence analysis of EEG band power and heart rate.
papers.summary: In healthy subjects, respiratory phase modulated brain-heart dynamics: inhale-hold increased gamma power, recurrence rate, and heart rate, while exhale-hold showed opposite effects, suggesting phase-dependent shifts between more stable and more variable neural activity states.

papers.title: DTI-ALPS as a marker of glymphatic function: Review of the literature findings, methodology, and interpretation.
papers.summary: This review of 393 DTI-ALPS studies summarizes its methodology, interpretation, and applications, concluding that DTI-ALPS is a sensitive but non-specific marker of white matter damage and neuroinflammation, with high reproducibility and translational potential for large-scale screening.

papers.title: Epi-Spec2State: Convolutional state space model via spectrogram image sequences for prediction-oriented seizure state classification in EEG signals.
papers.summary: The paper introduces Epi-Spec2State, a convolutional state space model using spectrogram image sequences for seizure state classification from EEG, achieving 96.40-96.60% accuracy and 98.20-98.30% specificity on a private SEEG dataset and outperforming nine state-of-the-art methods on public datasets.

papers.title: An EEG-based fatigue detection framework integrating interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling.
papers.summary: The study proposes the AXELLSTM framework for EEG-based cross-subject fatigue detection, integrating interpretable feature selection and an EfficientLSTM model, achieving a Macro-F1 of 0.7143 with a small model footprint, and identifying stable fatigue-related features and channels.

papers.title: A Novel Adversarial Approach for EEG Dataset Refinement: Enhancing Generalization Through Proximity-to-Boundary Scoring.
papers.summary: The paper presents a novel adversarial training framework using a proximity-to-boundary score to reduce the influence of noisy EEG samples, improving generalization by 1.43-6.66% on motor imagery datasets and 0.72-2.85% on a sleep stage dataset.

papers.title: Parent and child-reported acceptability and preference of pediatric home sleep apnea testing versus In-lab polysomnography: a pilot study.
papers.summary: This pilot study compared parent and child acceptability of home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) with EEG versus in-lab polysomnography in children, finding HSAT feasible and preferred by 60% of parents but only 33% of children, with sensor adjustments commonly needed.

papers.title: Aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on the jaw muscle electromyographic activities during sleep in young adult rats.
papers.summary: The study investigated the aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on jaw muscle activity during sleep in young adult rats, finding increased FosB expression in trigeminal premotor regions and enhanced noradrenergic fiber density, selectively increasing digastric muscle activity during arousal without altering sleep architecture.

papers.title: "Early Stratification of Risk for Poor Neurological Outcome After Cardiac Arrest Is Improved with Processed EEG Data".
papers.summary: This study evaluated machine learning models for early neurological risk stratification after cardiac arrest using clinical data alone, processed EEG metrics (suppression ratio and bispectral index) alone, and their combination in 913 patients. The combined model significantly improved discrimination for poor outcome (AUC 0.88 for long-term), outperforming either data source alone.

papers.title: Acute sleep deprivation rank-dependently enhances offensive aggression via the PVN in male mice.
papers.summary: In male mice, acute sleep deprivation selectively increased offensive aggression in dominant but not subordinate individuals, without affecting defensive aggression or social rank. This effect was associated with reduced mPFC and increased PVN neuronal activation, and chemogenetic inhibition of PVN neurons reversed the enhancement, indicating a PVN-dependent mechanism.

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Adaptive EEG Feature Selection and Weighting Method for Mental Workload Estimation in Rapid Serial Visual Presentation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a Multi-scale Adaptive Feature selection and Augmented Weighting (MAFA) framework for mental workload estimation from EEG in rapid serial visual presentation tasks. Using their own dataset, MAFA achieved higher classification accuracy than comparison methods and interpretable feature weights, with attention to posterior theta and alpha band activity.

papers.title: Physiologic and symptomatic burden across sleep-disordered breathing severity in men and women.
papers.summary: In a community cohort of 826 adults matched for severity, men and women with comparable sleep-disordered breathing severity exhibited different physiologic and symptomatic burdens: men with higher severity had more sleep disruption and daytime sleepiness, while women had more insomnia symptoms and lower quality of life. Significant sex-by-severity interactions were observed for sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, and daytime sleepiness.

papers.title: CEREBROVASCULAR EVENTS AND NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS WITH ALTERATIONS IN POLYSOMNOGRAPHIC INDICATORS FOLLOWING CARDIAC SURGERY.
papers.summary: In 104 patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, postoperative polysomnographic alterations (increased sleep latency and arousal index) correlated with cognitive impairment. Citicoline treatment (Group I) significantly improved MoCA scores and stabilized sleep parameters by day 30 compared to control, suggesting PSG parameters may serve as early markers of neurocognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment attenuates chronic stress-induced disruptions in the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, and brain.
papers.summary: In a chronic unpredictable mild stress mouse model, environmental enrichment reduced depressive-like behavior and reversed stress-induced gut microbiota changes, intestinal barrier disruption (restoring claudin-1 and reducing IL-6/NF-κB), and brain molecular alterations, suggesting it stabilizes the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

papers.title: Sleep and psychosis: An integrative review of conceptual and neurophysiological associations.
papers.summary: This integrative review summarizes conceptual and neurophysiological links between sleep processes (including dreaming and hypnagogic experiences) and psychosis, noting overlap in anterior cingulate and frontal regions but concluding direct neurobiological evidence is limited and identifying research gaps.

papers.title: Associations of Plasma Total Tau Level and MMSE Score With Polysomnographic Data in Middle-Aged Men With Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In middle-aged men with severe obstructive sleep apnea, plasma total tau levels positively correlated with apnea-hypopnea index, oxygen desaturation index, and arousal index, and negatively with N3 duration and mean oxygen saturation; MMSE scores showed opposite correlations, linking intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation to neurodegeneration and cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: In patients with atrial fibrillation and cognitive impairment, resting-state EEG showed reduced alpha-band functional connectivity (wPLI), which was independently associated with cognitive impairment (OR=0.44, AUC=0.814), supporting its potential as a biomarker for AF-related cognitive decline.

papers.title: Nocturnal heart rate variability in Parkinson's disease: associations with autonomic dysfunction, cognitive function, and mood symptoms.
papers.summary: Compared to healthy controls, Parkinson's disease patients showed lower nocturnal LF and LF/HF ratio and higher HF during sleep; in PD, better executive function and processing speed correlated with higher HF and lower LF/LF/HF, while autonomic symptoms were associated with worse cognition and mood.

papers.title: Association Between Nocturnal Oxygen Desaturation and the Severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 220 OSA patients found that AHI was positively associated with ODI and T90, and inversely with minimum and mean nocturnal SpO2, with all correlations significant after adjustment, suggesting related physiological patterns but not establishing causality or clinical utility beyond AHI.

papers.title: Negative BOLD response to interictal discharges in epilepsy using intracranial EEG-fMRI.
papers.summary: In 57 epilepsy patients with intracranial EEG-fMRI, positive BOLD responses to interictal discharges were significantly closer to seizure onset and IED-generating contacts than negative responses, while negative clusters overlapped more with the default mode network, indicating positive responses are preferable for presurgical localization.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture improves neurocognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation: an experimental study based on hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: In a rat model, electro-nape-acupuncture at GB20 and Extra for 14 days ameliorated chronic sleep deprivation-induced cognitive deficits, enhanced hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity in the dentate gyrus, and reversed CSD-induced reductions in DCX, Ki-67, spine density, and synaptic parameters.

papers.title: Association between habitual sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease: A cross-sectional study based on NHANES 2007-2018.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2007-2018 (N=29,692) found a significant positive association between longer sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease prevalence, persisting after adjustment, and advocates for including sleep duration in AD risk assessment; no mortality results are detailed.

papers.title: Adolescent depression recognition and symptom prediction based on multi-view EEG network: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study compared a multi-view adaptive graph convolutional network (MVA-GCN) using resting-state EEG to questionnaire-based models for adolescent depression, achieving 99.84% accuracy versus 86.43%, with occipital and fronto-central contributions and gamma connectivity increases and alpha power decreases as correlates, but brain-resilience correlations were not significant after correction.

papers.title: From bench to bedside: current evidence and prospects for acupuncture in managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.summary: This review examines acupuncture's potential in managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), synthesizing evidence that electroacupuncture and transcutaneous acupoint stimulation counteract PND risk factors through multi-target regulation centered on the gut-brain axis, reducing PND incidence and accelerating cognitive recovery.

papers.title: Armillariella tabescens polysaccharide targets microglial glycolysis to alleviate sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation through the mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.summary: This study isolated and characterized a polysaccharide from Armillariella tabescens (ATEP), showing it alleviates sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation by inhibiting mTOR signaling, which drives glycolytic metabolic reprogramming and microglial M1-to-M2 polarization, thereby improving cognitive function and reducing neurotoxic proteins in mice.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional Associations of Insomnia, Social Dysfunction, Suicidality, and Depressive Symptoms in Rural Adults with Schizophrenia: A Sex-Stratified Analysis.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 931 rural adults with schizophrenia found that insomnia, social dysfunction, and suicidality were each associated with depressive symptoms, with indirect associations via social dysfunction and suicidality; women reported higher symptom scores, but sex did not moderate these associations.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Seizure Disorders With and Without Interictal Epileptiform Discharges: A Retrospective Heart Rate Variability Analysis Using Archived Digital EEG Recordings.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared heart rate variability (HRV) among seizure patients with and without interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and a non-seizure control group, finding that seizure patients had lower vagally mediated HRV than controls, but IED presence was not associated with additional resting cardiac autonomic alterations.

papers.title: Cenobamate and Trazodone Combination Suppresses Seizures, EEG Alterations, Preserves Neuronal Architecture and Normalizes the BDNF/TrkB Expression in PTZ‑Kindled Mice.
papers.summary: This study in PTZ-kindled mice showed that combining cenobamate and trazodone suppressed seizures, normalized EEG alterations, preserved neuronal architecture, and restored BDNF/TrkB expression, outperforming monotherapies, suggesting a synergistically beneficial effect in epilepsy treatment.

papers.title: Evaluation of tirzepatide as an adjunct to buprenorphine for the treatment of opioid use disorder (TAB) trial: study design and rationale.
papers.summary: This paper describes the design and rationale of the TAB trial, a randomized controlled trial testing tirzepatide as an adjunct to buprenorphine for opioid use disorder. The primary outcome is 6-month buprenorphine treatment retention.

papers.title: Multidomain perioperative physiological vulnerability, longitudinal recovery patterns, and clinical outcomes after gastrointestinal cancer surgery in older adults.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of older adults undergoing gastrointestinal cancer surgery developed a Perioperative Aging Burden Index (PABI) from multidomain assessments. Higher PABI was associated with worse postoperative outcomes, and longitudinal recovery trajectories were identified.

papers.title: Associations of sleep duration variability and depressive symptoms with gastrointestinal disease among middle-aged and older adults: A cohort study.
papers.summary: This cohort study using CHARLS and HRS data found that greater sleep duration variability was associated with increased risk of gastrointestinal disease, with depression partially mediating this association.

papers.title: Transcranial direct current stimulation enhances cognitive performance and modulates QEEG beta- and theta-band power in patients undergoing whole-brain radiotherapy.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial found that transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) during whole-brain radiotherapy improved cognitive performance and reduced beta/theta power in QEEG, along with altered biomarker expression.

papers.title: Interplay of patent foramen ovale and atrial septum aneurysm in a nonagenarian patient presenting with platypnoea-orthodeoxia syndrome.
papers.summary: This case report describes a nonagenarian with platypnoea-orthodeoxia syndrome caused by a patent foramen ovale and atrial septum aneurysm, which was successfully treated with percutaneous PFO closure.
